uncited: SVO Node Location is a ray traversal algorithm that determines the specific octree node (internal or leaf) intersected by a ray at a given position, typically the ray origin or a point along the ray.
It solves the problem of mapping a continuous 3D ray position to a discrete Sparse Voxel Octree (SVO) node index, enabling subsequent shading or payload retrieval.

It differs from [Octree Node Lookup by Voxel](5120-octree-node-lookup-by-voxel.md) by explicitly handling ray geometry (intersection testing against child bounding boxes) to select the correct child branch, whereas the latter maps discrete voxel coordinates directly to node indices without ray-based intersection logic.
It builds on [Sparse Voxel Octree Ray Traversal](2451-sparse-voxel-octree-ray-traversal.md) by providing the foundational step of identifying the active node during traversal.
- This function iterates through all 8 children to find the one intersected by the ray closest to the origin (see *SVO First Node Selection* below).
This variant focuses on the initial step of selecting the correct child node of the current octree node that the ray intersects.
It differs from standard point-based lookup by using ray-box intersection tests (`svo_fast_forward_intersects_f3`) to determine which of the 8 children the ray enters.
It is chosen when the ray origin is not guaranteed to be inside a specific voxel or when precise entry point calculation is needed for shading.
This method traverses the SVO from root to find the leaf node containing a given 3D position, without using ray direction.
It differs from SVO Node Location by using simple binary mapping (front=1, back=0 for X/Y/Z) based on the position relative to the node center, rather than ray intersection tests.
It is chosen for point queries, neighbor lookups, or when the ray direction is irrelevant.
- **Time Complexity**: $O(D)$, where $D$ is the depth of the SVO.
SVO Node Location is a fundamental component of ray marching and ray tracing through Sparse Voxel Octrees.
